title: Gate a VCF 9.0 host commission behind its SDDC Manager precheck
prompt:
Implement `HostCommissionClient.java` as a single-file, JDK-only client for one VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager workflow: precheck a set of hosts, and commission them only if that precheck passes.

Start from the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json`. That contract was projected straight out of `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0` (commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`, blob `ff648cdf010715649b607f0edfa480b2c515e2a9`). The JSON specification at that tag is authoritative here - not a rendered documentation portal, and not the different revision of the same file that ships at the `9.1.0.0` tag. Use only the operationIds `validateHostCommissionSpec`, `getHostCommissionValidationByID` and `commissionHosts`. `validateCommissionHosts` on `/v1/hosts/validations/commissions` is deprecated at this tag and is out of scope.

Keep the public surface in `HostCommissionClient.java` exactly as declared - `TestMain` compiles against it. Both constructors already store their arguments and do no I/O; the two-argument constructor delegates with a five second poll interval and sixty polls.

`commission(List<HostCommissionSpec> hosts)` runs the whole workflow:

- Encode the hosts once, as a JSON array of `HostCommissionSpec` objects, and POST that array to `{baseUrl}/v1/hosts/validations` (`validateHostCommissionSpec`). A single host is still an array, never a bare object.
- The 202 body is a `Validation`. While its `executionStatus` is `IN_PROGRESS` or `CANCELLATION_IN_PROGRESS`, sleep the poll interval and re-read the validation with GET `{baseUrl}/v1/hosts/validations/{id}` (`getHostCommissionValidationByID`), using the `id` the server returned rather than any value of your own. Stop as soon as the status is one of `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `UNKNOWN`, `SKIPPED` or `CANCELLED`. If the poll budget runs out while the validation is still non-terminal, throw `SddcApiException` with `statusCode` 0 and `errorCode` `PRECHECK_NOT_TERMINAL`.
- The gate opens only for `executionStatus` `COMPLETED` together with `resultStatus` `SUCCEEDED`, which is what `PrecheckResult.passed()` reports. Every other terminal outcome - `WARNING` included - leaves it shut, and then nothing at all may be sent to POST `/v1/hosts`.
- Build a `PrecheckResult` either way: the validation's id, description, executionStatus and resultStatus, the number of poll requests you actually issued, and `failedChecks`, which holds the `description` of each entry of `validationChecks` whose `resultStatus` is not `SUCCEEDED`, in the order the server listed them.
- When the gate is shut, return a `CommissionOutcome` with `commissioned` false and a null `taskId`, `taskName` and `taskStatus`. When it opens, POST the same host array to `{baseUrl}/v1/hosts` (`commissionHosts`) and return `commissioned` true together with the `id`, `name` and `status` of the 202 `Task`.

Wire shape, which the harness inspects request by request:

- A request that carries a body sends `Content-Type: application/json` exactly, with no charset parameter. Every request sends `Accept: application/json`. The poll request has no body and therefore no `Content-Type`.
- None of the three operations declares a query parameter, so no request may carry a query string.
- `fqdn`, `username`, `password`, `storageType` and `networkPoolId` are required and always appear. `vvolStorageProtocolType`, `networkPoolName`, `sshThumbprint` and `sslThumbprint` appear only when the caller set them: an unset optional property must be absent from the encoded object, never sent as null, as an empty string, or as any other placeholder. Nothing outside the `HostCommissionSpec` schema goes on the wire.
- Reject a null or blank value with `IllegalArgumentException`, for a required constructor argument and for an optional fluent setter alike, so an empty value can never reach the wire in place of an omission.
- Any response other than 202 becomes an `SddcApiException` carrying the HTTP status in `statusCode`, the body's `errorCode`, and the body's `message` as the exception message.

Run the harness with `java TestMain.java` from the repository root. It starts a loopback stand-in for SDDC Manager on an ephemeral port, drives your client, and then asserts the mock's request log. Use the JDK only - no third-party libraries and no build tool. `Json.java` sits on the source path and you may use it to encode and decode JSON. `docs/`, `TestMain.java`, `MockSddcManager.java` and `Json.java` are protected: read them, but change nothing outside `HostCommissionClient.java`.

prerequisites.java: 22 or later (TestMain is launched in multi-file source mode)

scenario: Commissioning hosts is destructive, so SDDC Manager fronts it with a validation that runs asynchronously. The client must submit the precheck, follow it to a terminal execution status, and reach POST /v1/hosts only for COMPLETED plus SUCCEEDED - a WARNING, a FAILED, an error response or a validation that never settles must all leave the estate untouched.
environment_note: MockSddcManager binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port and builds its routing table from the protected docs/contract.json, so it serves only validateHostCommissionSpec, getHostCommissionValidationByID and commissionHosts and answers anything else 404. It applies no gating of its own - POST /v1/hosts is answered whenever it is sent - and appends every exchange to a JSON Lines request log in a temporary directory that TestMain reads back. No route in the seed reaches a live VMware endpoint.
constraint: The harness asserts the request log independently of the client's return values: the operation sequence, the paths including the server-issued validation id, exact header values, that no request carries a query string or lands outside the contract, that both request bodies are JSON arrays whose objects hold exactly the properties that were set - unset optional fields omitted rather than sent empty or null - and that no request reaches POST /v1/hosts on any run where the precheck did not pass.
